title: Case: A crated van engine has not arrived two days after its delivery date
context: A reconditioned engine ordered from a trade parts warehouse was due on a Monday. The consignee has a second, smaller order with the same carrier and has written about both.
initial_request: Right. Engine. DL-991. Two days late and nobody at Tallowmere or Plover bloody Arc can tell me where it is. Rang both yesterday, both said 'in progress', which is bollocks. My van's been up on Kell's lift at Minnow Lane Motors since last Thursday with the old lump out of it. He's got a bay blocked, he's turning jobs away, and he's told me straight it comes off the lift Friday, engine or no engine. Get a trace on it NOW and get it on a van tomorrow. Wiper motor turned up, ta.

events.body: DL-991 (TG-991): one crated reconditioned van engine, 240 kg. Shipper Tallowmere Goods trade parts warehouse. Collection booked Thursday 5 Nov, delivery to consignee G. Hartigan Monday 9 Nov, tail-lift vehicle.
Statement reminder: invoice BB-8102 for DL-977 falls due on 12 Nov. Please disregard if already paid. Plover Arc Logistics, moving what matters.

DL-991: collection on 5 Nov not completed. Vehicle attended 15:20; the shipper's warehouse had no crate staged and no forklift operator on site. Nothing was loaded and the consignment has never been in our network. Rebook notice sent to the shipper 5 Nov 16:05, no answer. We can only rebook on the shipper's request. That is Warehouse dispatch, Tallowmere Goods, through their Warehouse work queue.

events.from: Freight portal notifications, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: Automated status: DL-991 - Booked, in progress. Estimated delivery 9 Nov. This is an automated message; replies are not read.
Engine was meant to be here today. Where is it.
Thanks for your message. We aim to reply within one working day. Did you know you can follow your delivery live in the app?
WINTER TRADE EVENT. 15% off brake kits, batteries and workshop consumables until Sunday. Free carriage on orders over 150. Unsubscribe at any time.
And while you're at it DL-968, the wiper motor, has said out for delivery since Friday. That's not here either.
DL-968 delivered 10 Nov 11:12, signed G. Hartigan.

Freight planner: DL-991, yeah, I've got it as booked, in progress, ETA the ninth. I can't see where it physically is from this screen. If the customer's chasing I'd just put a trace in with the Parcel trace team and let them find it.
Return RA-5530 for order TG-940 is approved. A label will follow from the Return label team.

Right. Engine. DL-991. Two days late and nobody at Tallowmere or Plover bloody Arc can tell me where it is. Rang both yesterday, both said 'in progress', which is bollocks. My van's been up on Kell's lift at Minnow Lane Motors since last Thursday with the old lump out of it. He's got a bay blocked, he's turning jobs away, and he's told me straight it comes off the lift Friday, engine or no engine. Get a trace on it NOW and get it on a van tomorrow. Wiper motor turned up, ta.

acceptable_actions.summary: Tell the shipper the 5 Nov collection of DL-991 failed at their warehouse and ask them to stage the crate and request a rebooked collection from Collections control.

must: Contacts Warehouse dispatch, Tallowmere Goods on the Warehouse work queue about DL-991.

States that the 5 Nov collection was not completed because no crate was staged and no forklift operator was on site, that the engine has never entered the carrier's network, and that Collections control's rebook notice of 5 Nov is unanswered.
Asks Warehouse dispatch to stage the crate and request a new collection from Collections control, and to confirm the date.

Tells Warehouse dispatch that the consignee's van has been on a third party's workshop lift with the old engine out since 5 Nov, that the garage will take it off the lift on Friday 13 Nov, and that he has been told 'in progress' by both companies, so the rebook is treated as urgent.
must_not: Opens or requests a trace with the Parcel trace team for a consignment that was never collected.
Tells Gus Hartigan the engine is in transit, in progress, or will be on a van tomorrow.
Promises a delivery date, or compensation for the garage's lost bay.
Books or recommends a different carrier on the shipper's behalf.
Takes any further action on DL-968, which is delivered, or on the unrelated billing, returns and newsletter messages.
expected.reference_message: Urgent, DL-991 / TG-991, crated reconditioned van engine for G. Hartigan. Plover Arc's Collections control reports that the collection booked for 5 Nov was not completed: their vehicle attended at 15:20, no crate was staged and there was no forklift operator on site, so nothing was loaded. The engine has never been in the carrier's network. They sent your team a rebook notice on 5 Nov at 16:05 and have had no answer, and they can only rebook at the shipper's request. Please stage the crate, request a new collection from Collections control, and tell me the date they give you. This cannot wait: the consignee's van has been on a workshop lift at an independent garage with the old engine removed since 5 Nov, the garage has a bay blocked and says the van comes off the lift on Friday 13 Nov whether the engine has arrived or not, and he has twice been told 'in progress' when it had not moved. I have promised him no date.

rationale: Most of the thread is about other shipments, an automated status and a newsletter. The one fact that decides it is the Collections control note: the engine was never collected and only the shipper can ask for a rebook. A trace, which both the customer and the Freight planner suggest, has nothing to find. The message goes to Warehouse dispatch with the garage's Friday deadline.

review.note: The coordinator contacted Warehouse dispatch on the Warehouse work queue with the failed collection facts and the Friday deadline, and raised no trace.
